cut.title: Cut
steps: Anchor yourself and the crew member to a handrail or foot loops.
Put on gloves.
Press gauze firmly on the cut for 10 minutes. Do not lift it to check.
Clean around it with sterile water and close it with closure strips.
Cover with a dressing. Check it again in 2 hours.
help: Still bleeding after 10 minutes of firm pressure
Deep or gaping, or you can see fat or bone
Numb or weak past the cut
cut.space: Blood does not drip. It balls up on the skin and can float off. Catch it with gauze.
cut.kit: Gloves, gauze, sterile water, closure strips, dressing

puncture.title: Puncture wound
steps: Anchor yourself and the crew member.
Do not pull out anything that is stuck in the skin.
Press gauze around it, not on it, to slow bleeding.
Pad around the object and tape it so it cannot move.
Call ground before taking anything out.
puncture.space: Loose fragments can float into eyes and air filters. Bag every piece.

burn.title: Burn
steps: Get away from the heat source and switch it off.
Cool the burn with a cold wet towel for 20 minutes.
Take off rings, watch or tight clothing near it before it swells.
Cover loosely with a burn dressing.
Do not pop blisters or put cream on it.
help: Bigger than the palm of a hand
On the face, hands, joints or groin
burn.space: Water will not run over the burn. Soak a towel and hold it on.

fracture.title: Possible broken bone
steps: Keep it still. Do not try to straighten it.
Splint it as you found it, past the joint above and below.
Check past the injury: warm, pink, and they can feel your touch.
Wrap a cold pack in cloth and hold it on for 15 minutes.
Pain medicine from the kit, as the flight surgeon set out.
help: Cold, numb or blue past the injury
fracture.space: Strap the splinted limb to the body or a rail so it cannot drift and knock things.
fracture.kit: Splint, elastic wrap, cold pack, pain medicine
fracture.limits: No exercise with this limb and no spacewalks until ground clears it.

dislocation.title: Dislocated joint
steps: Do not try to push it back in.
Support it in the position you found it, with a sling or splint.
Check past the joint: warm, pink, and they can feel your touch.
Cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15 minutes.
Call ground. They talk you through putting it back.
help: Cold, numb or blue past the joint
dislocation.space: Without weight pulling on it, a joint can look fine. Compare it with the other side.
dislocation.kit: Sling, splint, cold pack, pain medicine
dislocation.limits: No exercise with this joint until ground clears it.

sprain.title: Sprain or strain
steps: Stop using it.
Cold pack wrapped in cloth, 15 minutes, every 2 to 3 hours.
Wrap it with an elastic bandage. Firm, not tight.
Check past it: warm, pink, and they can feel your touch.
Move it gently after 2 days if the pain allows.
help: A pop, then it will not work
sprain.space: Muscles are weaker after months in space, so they tear more easily. Go easy on it.
sprain.kit: Cold pack, elastic wrap, pain medicine
sprain.limits: No heavy exercise with this part for 3 days.

head.title: Head injury
steps: Stop all work. Strap in and stay still.
Ask: what is your name, where are you, what day is it?
Check the pupils with a light. Both should be the same size.
Cold pack on the bump for 15 minutes.
Someone checks on them every 2 hours for the next day.
help: One pupil bigger than the other
Clear fluid from the nose or ears
head.space: Head-down fluid shift already raises head pressure in space. Treat any knock seriously.
head.limits: No spacewalks, exercise or pain medicine that thins the blood until ground clears it.

eye.title: Something in the eye
steps: Do not rub it.
Hold the eyewash cup over the eye and rinse for 5 minutes.
Blink. Look up, down, left and right.
Check with a light and mirror. Lift the speck off with a wet swab.
Still hurts? Tape a pad over it and rest the eye.
eye.space: Dust and metal flakes do not settle. They float. This is one of the most common injuries on the ISS.
eye.kit: Eyewash cup, saline, penlight, swab, eye pad

nosebleed.title: Nosebleed
steps: Lean forward, not back.
Pinch the soft part of the nose for 10 to 15 minutes. Breathe through the mouth.
Catch blood with gauze so it does not float.
Cold pack on the bridge of the nose.
No blowing the nose for a few hours.
help: Came after a hit to the head
nosebleed.space: Fluid shifts to the head in space, so nosebleeds are more common. Blood can float into the eyes.

chest.title: Chest pain
steps: Stop all activity. Strap in and rest.
Take heart rate and blood pressure now, and every 5 minutes.
Put on oxygen if breathing is hard.
Aspirin from the kit, if the flight surgeon protocol says so.
Call ground now with the readings.
help: Pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back
Short of breath, sweaty or faint
Heart rate very fast or uneven
chest.space: An AED works in space. Strap the crew member down first so the shock does not push them away.
chest.kit: Blood pressure cuff, oxygen mask, aspirin, AED

back.title: Back pain
steps: Curl up: pull your knees to your chest and hold for 30 seconds.
Repeat 5 times, then stretch out slowly.
Warm pack on the sore spot for 15 minutes.
Pain medicine from the kit if needed.
No heavy lifting on the resistance machine today.
help: Pain after a hit or fall
back.space: The spine stretches up to 5 cm in space, which strains the discs. Most crew get back pain early on.

nail.title: Fingernail injury
steps: Clean the finger with sterile water.
Trim any loose part of the nail so it cannot catch.
Cover with a small dressing and tape.
Keep it dry. Change the dressing every day.
help: Red, hot or pus under the nail
nail.space: Spacewalk gloves press on the fingertips and can lift nails off.
nail.kit: Nail clippers, sterile water, dressing, tape
nail.limits: No spacewalks until the nail heals and the glove fit is checked.

ear.title: Ear pressure injury
steps: Stop any pressure change: hold the airlock or suit pressure where it is.
Swallow, yawn, or pinch the nose and blow gently to even the pressure.
Do not put anything in the ear.
Pain medicine from the kit if it aches.
Test hearing: rub fingers by each ear and compare.
help: Blood or fluid from the ear
Hearing loss that does not come back
ear.space: Airlock and suit pressure changes squeeze the eardrum. A head cold in space makes it worse, because the sinuses cannot drain.
ear.limits: No spacewalks or airlock use until the ear clears.

kidney.title: Kidney stone
steps: Drink 2 to 3 litres of water through the day.
Pain medicine from the kit, as the flight surgeon set out.
Collect urine in the sample bag to catch the stone.
Take temperature. A fever changes the plan.
Rest strapped in. Ground runs an ultrasound with you.
help: Pain that medicine does not touch
kidney.space: Calcium lost from bones in space goes through the kidneys and can form stones.
kidney.kit: Pain medicine, urine sample bags, thermometer, ultrasound

sick.title: Space sickness
steps: Strap in and keep your head still.
Fix your eyes on one point. Line your body up with the module floor.
Anti-sickness medicine from the kit.
Keep a sick bag in hand. Sip water slowly.
Rest. Most crew feel better in 2 to 3 days.
help: Cannot keep water down for a day
Dizzy, dry mouth, very little urine
sick.space: Most new astronauts get it. The inner ear and eyes disagree about which way is up. Vomit floats, so bag it.
sick.limits: No spacewalks while sick. Vomit inside a helmet can choke you.

bends.title: Decompression sickness
steps: Tell ground now.
Put on the oxygen mask: pure oxygen, tight fit.
Get back in the suit and raise its pressure. The suit becomes a pressure chamber.
Stay still. Do not rub or exercise the sore joint.
Check vision, strength and feeling every 10 minutes.
help: Numb or weak arms or legs
bends.space: Spacewalk suits run at low pressure. Nitrogen in the blood can form bubbles, most often in the shoulders and elbows.
bends.kit: Oxygen mask, suit pressure kit, pain medicine
bends.limits: No spacewalks until ground clears it.

radiation.title: Radiation sickness
steps: Go to the storm shelter now: the area walled with water and supplies.
Write down your dosimeter reading.
Anti-sickness medicine from the kit.
Drink water. Rest.
Ground will ask for a blood sample in the next days.
help: Vomiting within hours of the dose
radiation.space: Outside Earth's magnetic field, a solar storm can deliver a large dose in hours.
radiation.kit: Dosimeter, anti-sickness medicine, blood sample kit
radiation.limits: Stay in the shelter until the storm passes.

air.title: Breathing trouble
steps: Move to another module with a working fan.
Put on the oxygen mask.
Check the CO₂ reading on the ship display.
Smoke? Press the fire alarm and close the hatch behind you.
Check blood oxygen on the finger sensor. It should be 95% or more.
air.space: Air does not rise or mix by itself. Without a fan, your breath forms a CO₂ bubble around your head.
air.kit: Oxygen mask, finger sensor, smoke mask

cold.title: Cold injury
steps: Warm the fingers slowly: hold them in your armpits.
Do not rub them.
Soak in warm water, 37 to 39 °C, for 20 minutes if you can.
Wrap each finger loosely in dry gauze.
Pain medicine from the kit. Rewarming hurts.
cold.space: In shadow, spacewalk gloves face −150 °C. If a glove heater fails, fingertips go first.
cold.limits: No spacewalks until the fingers are checked.

crush.title: Crush injury
steps: Free it gently.
Check the shape: bent or out of place means treat it as a break.
Cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15 minutes.
Check the nail: dark blood underneath needs the flight surgeon.
Tape it to the next finger if it hurts to move.
crush.space: Hatches and heavy gear still have full mass. They move slowly but stop hard.

tooth.title: Toothache
steps: Rinse the mouth with warm salt water.
Pain medicine from the kit.
Lost filling? Pack it with temporary filling from the dental kit.
Clove oil on a cotton swab for the pain.
Soft food. Chew on the other side.
tooth.space: The nearest dentist is months away. Crew learn basic dental care before flight.
tooth.kit: Dental kit, temporary filling, clove oil, pain medicine

allergy.title: Allergic reaction
steps: Get away from whatever caused it.
Allergy medicine from the kit.
Lips, tongue or throat swelling, or hard to breathe? Use the adrenaline pen in the thigh now.
Oxygen mask on.
Strap in. Someone stays with them.
help: Swelling in the mouth or throat
allergy.space: New foods, cleaning wipes and lab chemicals are common causes on board.
allergy.kit: Allergy medicine, adrenaline pen, oxygen mask

rash.title: Skin rash
steps: Clean the skin gently and pat dry.
Hydrocortisone cream, thin layer, twice a day.
Loose clothing over it.
Take a photo for the flight surgeon.
rash.space: Skin gets thin and dry in space and heals more slowly. Rashes are one of the most common complaints.

faint.title: Fainting
steps: Strap them in so they cannot drift into anything.
Check they are breathing and take a pulse.
Take heart rate and blood pressure.
When awake: drink water with a salt tablet.
Rest for an hour before moving around.
help: Does not wake within a minute
faint.space: Blood volume drops in space, so the heart has less to work with. Hard exercise can tip it over.
faint.kit: Blood pressure cuff, salt tablets, water

bruise.title: Bruise
steps: Cold pack wrapped in cloth, 15 minutes.
Check it moves normally and is not misshapen.
Compare it with the other side.
Check again in 2 hours. Repeat the cold pack if it swells.
bruise.space: Loose objects keep moving in space. Strap down whatever hit you.

shock.title: Electric shock
steps: Cut the power before you touch them.
Check they are awake and breathing.
Take heart rate. Watch for an uneven beat.
Look for burns where the current went in and out. Cover them.
Call ground now, even if they feel fine.
help: Not breathing or no pulse: start CPR and get the AED
shock.space: For CPR, strap them to the floor and brace your feet on the ceiling.
shock.kit: AED, burn dressing, blood pressure cuff

steps: Stop what you are doing and anchor yourself.
Look at it and compare with the other side: swelling, bleeding, shape.
Check they can move it and feel your touch.
Cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15 minutes if it swells or hurts.
Tell the flight surgeon on the next call.
help: Numb, cold or blue past the injury
general.space: Strap down anything loose first. Tools and blood both float.
